rationale: bugs_open/231 candidate 3, and the census instrument its open items require. The proven mechanism: ExtractActionInputs applies spec.Defaults first and every later strategy except Strategy 0 skips a populated field, so against a defaulted field a static config value, a numeric/boolean literal, and the deprecated *_field bridge are all silently dead, and a defaulted field outside Required+Optional is dead to every config shape (strategies 0/4/5 iterate Required+Optional only). Two live faces already shipped damage (the pre-348 static purpose 'logo' that produced months of hero-shaped logos; the pre-380 unresolvable dotted purpose). This adds the offline detector as a fifth mode on cmd/config-key-audit (a flag, not a second binary, per the council's own 2026-07-28 precedent recorded in that file's header), walking live definitions with validation.WalkSteps and classifying every config entry bound to a defaulted field by the exact resolver arm that kills it. Exit 1 only on dead entries whose value MISMATCHES the default; matching statics and dotted_conditional (arm-2 exposure, undecidable offline) are reported, never fatal, so the signal stays narrow. Calibrated on BOTH live faces as committed tests against the real registry. First fleet run (2026-08-11, 182 agents, 62 specs with Defaults): 24 dead-mismatched, of which read-path verification confirmed exactly 4 as live damage - four auditor agents' distinctive audit_source statics on write_audit_findings are dead and every finding they have ever filed is labelled 'design-audit' (filed in 231, notified in 213, LANDMINES entry synced). The tool's finding deliberately asserts the INPUTS path only; the header and wrapper carry the direct-config-read caveat that separated the 4 real from the 20 false.

plan.summary: One new mode on the existing config-key-audit binary (--default-shadowed-keys), its pure-check tests including calibration on both of 231's live faces, a defaults field on --specs, and the standard wrapper script. No runtime code changes; the resolver is untouched.

edits.rationale: The pure check, separated from I/O like findUnregisteredActions/findSuspiciousKeys so fixture tests exercise it. Classification mirrors ExtractActionInputs' arms exactly (Strategy 0's dot test is strings.Contains(v,"."); strategies 0/4/5 iterate Required+Optional only; every skip is has-value, which a Default guarantees). Classes: static_string, non_string_literal, composite_literal, deprecated_bridge, unextractable_field (dead), dotted_conditional (informational - resolvability is a runtime fact). One dead() definition shared by exit rule and summary. Refuses an empty agent export AND an empty Defaults registry (a dropped blank import must fail loudly).

Behaviour tests drive the pure check with SYNTHETIC specs (one per class boundary, plus negatives: non-defaulted fields and unknown actions are silent, nested loop steps are walked per bugs_open/144). Calibration tests use the REAL registry to pin both motivating cases: the pre-348 pageflow static fires static_string/mismatch, asset-deployer's input_data.purpose reports dotted_conditional. If deploy_image_asset's Defaults legitimately change, calibration fails and must be updated deliberately, citing the change - same contract as the three pinned tests in the actions package.

Dispatch the new flag; document it in the usage header alongside its siblings. specDump gains a defaults field so --specs answers the census's arm-3 question (what does every spec default) from the binary rather than a source grep, which bugs_open/223's var-blindness has burned three consumers with. Additive JSON only; grep shows no script consumes --specs, and the default-mode output is byte-identical.

Standard wrapper, identical export query and error discipline to audit-single-owner-actions.sh (WalkSteps descends into sub-workflows, so the SQL must not try to - bugs_open/144). Human-readable summary separates dead findings (with MISMATCH tag) from conditional dotted bindings; --json for joins. Carries the direct-config-read caveat in its header so a consumer cannot read a finding as damage without the check.
edits.sketch:
WORKFLOWS_JSON="$(psql_q "SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('type', type, 'workflow', default_config->'workflow')) FROM agent_definitions WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND is_active AND default_config ? 'workflow';")"
printf '%s' "$WORKFLOWS_JSON" | go run ./cmd/config-key-audit --default-shadowed-keys

grounded_in: bugs_open/231: 'against a defaulted field, only a Strategy-0 dotted path can win' - the general rule this detector classifies by, pinned by three committed characterisation tests that EXECUTE the real resolver.

action_inputs.go:544-574 (Strategy 0: only multi-segment dotted strings, strings.Contains(pathStr,".")), :585/:597 (Strategies 1/2 skip alreadyResolved), :609 (Strategy 3 skips hasValue), :661-693 (Strategy 4 iterates allFields, skips hasValue), :714-733 (Strategy 5 non-string scalars, skips hasValue). allFields = Required+Optional at :549-550, which is what makes unextractable_field a class.

cmd/config-key-audit/main.go header: 'It is a FLAG rather than a second binary because the council gate's editquality and reuse_agent seats both objected to the second binary independently (2026-07-28, corr 07cf67c6)' - the precedent this follows.

First run, live fleet 2026-08-11: 182 agents decoded, 62/164 specs with Defaults, 232 defaulted fields; 24 dead-mismatched / 75 dead-matching / 96 dotted_conditional. Read-path verification: 20/24 honoured via direct config reads (each read line cited in bugs_open/231's 2026-08-11 section); 4/24 real - write_audit_findings_action.go:495 inputs.Get("audit_source"), zero site_work_items rows fleet-wide carry any of the four auditors' intended labels, and the contradiction row item_type='audit_finding_brief_fidelity' + audit_source='design-audit' (2026-07-24) settles attribution.

The narrowness argument for exit-1-on-mismatch-only: main.go's suspiciousKeyChars comment - 'A broader set would turn this into a linter people learn to ignore, which is the state that lets the next real one through.' 75 live matching statics would otherwise fail every run from day one.
plan.risks: 1) A consumer may read a dead-mismatched finding as live damage when the action reads config directly (20 of the first run's 24) - mitigated three ways: the caveat is in the file header, the wrapper output, and RUNBOOK 209 §11's standing check; the finding text says 'dead on the inputs path', not 'ignored'. 2) The classifier is a second copy of the resolver's semantics and can drift - mitigated by the calibration tests executing the REAL registry and by 231's own pinned tests executing the real resolver; if candidate 2 ever changes the resolver, both flip together and must be updated deliberately. 3) The defaults field on --specs changes that JSON shape - additive only, and grep over scripts/ and docs shows no consumer of --specs output today. 4) matches_default compares JSON float64 against Go typed ints - normalised via toFloat64 for all numeric widths; non-numeric composites fall to reflect.DeepEqual, where a false negative merely downgrades a finding from 'matching' to 'MISMATCH', i.e. fails loud, not silent.
